messages:
maria: Heads-up — finance noticed a spike of small refunds on acct_44321 between 2026-04-02T02:10Z and 02:18Z. Total refunded $1,420 across 7 refunds. Cardholder filed a chargeback for $420 (card **** **** **** 1111). Need evidence + recommendation on hold.
billing-bot: Chargeback created — CB87654321 for txn `T20260402-7b2` — reason: cardholder_dispute — dispute window closes 2026-06-01. Case link: https://redwood.internal/disputes/CB87654321
jon: quick scan shows refunds came from our partner integration `automation_bot` via vendor QuickRefunds. API calls look like batched refunds from webhook handler. Example request: `POST /v1/refunds {"charge":"T20260401-xx","amount":60}`.
kevin: integration metadata: integration_id=quickrefunds-33, API_KEY=quick_rfn_77. Vendor last reported key rotation 2026-04-01 (per their dashboard). The key used in logs is the older key value. Possible replay/compromise.
maria: server logs: origin IPs 203.0.113.45 and 203.0.113.46 (ASN: AS64500) — geo Singapore. Customer billing address on file is USA. Webhook delivery shows 200 OK for all refund callbacks.
jon: KYC: acct_44321 business name "Cedar & Co" (NY), billing email billing@cedar.example.com. Last console access for account was 2026-03-29 from IP 198.51.100.77 (Toronto). No recent CS portal requests.
kevin: Note: refund flows don't require CVV and are allowed for partners. That weakens our onus in chargeback defense.
maria: Suggested next steps: 1) pause `automation_bot` integration and revoke key `quick_rfn_77`, 2) upload evidence packet to disputes, 3) open security ticket with QuickRefunds and ask for their audit logs + key rotation proof, 4) place provisional hold on acct_44321 pending vendor reply.
jon: I've placed a provisional hold HLD-20260402-09 at 2026-04-02T03:01Z and notified CS to pause communication.
billing-bot: Evidence packet uploaded: https://redwood.internal/evidence/CB87654321 (access: finance, disputes, legal).
kevin: @legal-team — please advise whether to fight the chargeback or offer partial settlement. We can attach API request/response logs, timestamps, IP geos, vendor key rotation notice. Customer-facing proof is weak without additional partner logs.
legal-team: Reviewing. Send preserved logs and chain of custody for the webhook handler. If QuickRefunds can produce signed audit logs showing actioning by their account, we'll have stronger grounds to contest.
maria: I'll assemble merchant response draft with: txn/refund IDs, timestamps, request bodies, IP geolocation, KYC snapshot, and partner rotation confirmation. Will add to the evidence packet when ready.
jon: thanks — keeping this thread as single source. Will update when QuickRefunds replies. :eyes:
